 \le Cn^{3/4}\log n.$$ Types with more than half as many rows as line sites have zero sweep operator by matching annihilation, and are omitted. For a remaining profile put $D_0=\sum_i\log(D_{\mu_i}r_i)$.

<a id="rec:smoothed-eighth"></a>
Fix a nontrivial surviving parent type $\lambda$ and write $L=\log D_\lambda$. Lemma <a href="#rec:smoothed-grid-fourth" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="rec:smoothed-grid-fourth">73</a>, together with regular multiplicity, gives $$a_\lambda:=\operatorname{Tr}|(JI)_\lambda|^4
 \le A_0/D_\lambda,\qquad
 A_0=\exp\{(1+\eta)D_0+E_d\},\quad
 \eta=C_1/\sqrt d,$$ where $E_d=n^{1-1/200}$ absorbs $Cn m^{-1/40}$ for all sufficiently large $d$. The compression $(JI)_\lambda$ is a contraction. If its singular values are $u_j$, then $\sum_j u_j^8\le\sum_j u_j^4=a_\lambda$ and $\sum_j u_j^8\le(\sum_j u_j^4)^2=a_\lambda^2$. Consequently $$\label{rec:smoothed-eighth}
 D_\lambda\operatorname{Tr}|(JI)_\lambda|^8
 \le A_0\min\{1,A_0/D_\lambda\}.$$

<a id="rec:smoothed-profile-saving"></a>
Set $p_d=(1+A/\sqrt d)p'$ and $h=p_d/8\ge1$. Resolve $|Y|^h|X^*|^h$ into its profile terms. A term has the form $B_J(JI)A_I$, with $A_I,B_J$ supported on the indicated projections. The product of their operator norms is at most $e^{-hD_0/p'}$. The ideal property of Schatten norms and <a href="#rec:smoothed-eighth" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rec:smoothed-eighth">[rec:smoothed-eighth]</a> therefore show that the logarithm of its eighth power norm, after multiplication by $D_\lambda$, is at most $$\label{rec:smoothed-profile-saving}
 -\frac{A-C_1}{\sqrt d}D_0+E_d
 +\min\{0,(1+\eta)D_0+E_d-L\}.$$ This bound is independent of the size of $p'$.

<a id="rec:smoothed-powered-moment"></a>
Choose $A>C_1+8$. In the dense range $k>n^{1-1/400}$, <a href="#rec:band-dimension-lower" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rec:band-dimension-lower">[rec:band-dimension-lower]</a> gives $L\ge c n^{1-1/400}$. Hence $E_d=o(L/\sqrt d)$ and $\log N_d=o(L/\sqrt d)$, with thresholds independent of $p'$. If $D_0\ge L/4$, the first two terms in <a href="#rec:smoothed-profile-saving" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rec:smoothed-profile-saving">[rec:smoothed-profile-saving]</a> are at most $-c_1L/\sqrt d$. If $D_0<L/4$, then $(1+\eta)D_0+E_d\le L/2$ for large $d$, and the same expression is at most $-L/3$. Thus every profile term $F_\gamma$ satisfies $$D_\lambda\|F_\gamma\|_8^8
 \le e^{-c_2L/\sqrt d}.$$ The triangle inequality, followed by <a href="#rec:smoothed-profile-count" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rec:smoothed-profile-count">[rec:smoothed-profile-count]</a>, gives $$\label{rec:smoothed-powered-moment}
 D_\lambda\big\||Y|^h|X^*|^h\big\|_8^8
 \le N_d^8e^{-c_2L/\sqrt d}\le1.$$ All norms in this paragraph are on the single parent irreducible.

Apply Lemma <a href="#lem:positive-power-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:positive-power-comparison">9</a> with $q=8$: <a id="rec:smoothed-power-interpolation"></a>$$\label{rec:smoothed-power-interpolation}
 \|YX\|_p\le
 \big\||Y|^{p/8}|X^*|^{p/8}\big\|_8^{8/p},\qquad p\ge8.$$ Combining this with <a href="#rec:smoothed-powered-moment" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rec:smoothed-powered-moment">[rec:smoothed-powered-moment]</a> yields $\sum_r s_r(T_n|_{V_\lambda})^{p_d}\le D_\lambda^{-1}$. Since the singular values decrease, their first $r$ terms imply the required bound $(D_\lambda r)^{-1/p_d}$.

In the sparse range $1\le k\le n^{1-1/400}$, use <a href="#rec:forest-sparse-general" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rec:forest-sparse-general">[rec:forest-sparse-general]</a> with $\delta=1/400$ and $\log(D_\lambda r)\le2k\log n$. It suffices to keep all exponents at least $2/c_{1/400}$, which is achieved by increasing the common finite base exponent. Lemma <a href="#lem:finitegap" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:finitegap">5</a> supplies a sufficiently large common base exponent for the finitely many nonconstant blocks and singular indices at those sizes. The trivial block has $D_\lambda=r=1$ and singular value one, and the killed blocks have singular value zero, so both satisfy the statement directly.

Finally the large-size threshold depends only on the absolute constants in the overlap and dimension bounds, not on the finite base exponent. Lemma <a href="#lem:dyadic-exponents" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:dyadic-exponents">18</a>, with $\gamma=1/2$, bounds the product of $1+A/\sqrt d$ along every rounded-halving branch. Hence $\sup_d p_d<\infty$. ◻

</details>

The indexed power bounds of Sections <a href="#sec:convex-grid" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:convex-grid">[sec:convex-grid]</a>–<a href="#sec:smoothed-grid" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:smoothed-grid">17</a> now give the same fixed-sweep mixing consequence by the conversion in Section <a href="#sec:spectral-conversion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:spectral-conversion">4</a>. Their usable operator exponents are, respectively, $10^{-8}c$, $\alpha$, and $1/\sup_dp_d$. For any of these exponents $a>0$, an integer $R$ with $2aR\ge3$ makes the regular contribution $D_\lambda\|T_n(\lambda)^R\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2$ of each nontrivial nonzero block at most $D_\lambda^{-1}$. The sign block vanishes, and Lemma <a href="#lem:degrees" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:degrees">8</a> makes the sum tend to zero. Thus $R$ forward sweeps, or $Rd$ physical shuffles, converge to uniform in total variation. The matching order lower bound is Lemma <a href="#lem:support" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:support">[lem:support]</a>.
